title: Akihabara on Foot
blurb: Walk Akihabara under the real sun: Chuo-dori's signs and wall prints, the lanes of parts shops and arcades, and up the hill to Kanda Myojin and Nikolai-do.

travel.name: Akihabara, Electric Town exit 電気街口
Radio Kaikan, the corner ラジオ会館前
Kanda Myojin, the gate 隨神門
Nikolai-do, the gate ニコライ堂前

npcs.name: Yuto 悠斗
npcs.role: Parts shop owner パーツ屋
idle: After the war this was a black market for radio parts, under the tracks. Then TVs, then PCs, then games.
Junk boxes still: a hundred yen a cable. {time}.

npcs.name: Mai 舞
idle: お帰りなさいませ! Welcome home. Flyers, flyers. The cafe's on the fifth floor.
We say 'welcome home', not 'welcome'. It's a game everyone plays.

npcs.name: Taku 拓
idle: Junk Street. The shops here sell cartridges by the kilo, if you know where to look.
The arcade by the station has a cabinet from 1987 that still eats coins. {sun_line}

npcs.name: Emi 恵美
idle: Kanda Myojin is Akihabara's shrine. We sell charms to protect your computer. Really.
The festival is in May, in odd years. The portable shrines go right down Chuo-dori.

quests.title: Electric Town
talk: Welcome to Akiba! I'm Yuto. My father sold radio parts under these tracks; I sell everything else.
Chuo-dori is the main street; the lanes behind it are where things happen. Mai hands out flyers on the corner.

quests.title: Welcome home
talk: Every weekend afternoon Chuo-dori closes to cars: 歩行者天国, the pedestrians' heaven. Come back on a Sunday.
Taku knows the lanes. He's on Junk Street, north of the arcades.

quests.title: Junk Street
talk: Look up at the blade signs: パーツ, 中古, 買取, レトロゲーム. Every floor a different shop.
Pick a door and climb. In Akiba the best shop is always on the top floor, and the lift is always broken.

quests.title: Kanda Myojin
talk: Up the hill from Electric Town: Kanda Myojin, the shrine of Edo's merchants, now of its programmers.
And further, over the river, Nikolai-do's green dome. Go and listen for its bells.

areas.name: 秋葉原
areas.note: Electric Town: where a game sends you to buy parts and play retro games

spots.name: Zuishinmon 随神門
lines: Kanda Myojin has watched over Kanda, Nihonbashi and Akihabara since Edo. Akihabara's shops come here for New Year blessings on their computers.
The gate dates from 1975; the hall behind it, all vermilion concrete, from 1934. It survived the war's fires.

spots.name: Nikolai-do ニコライ堂
lines: The Holy Resurrection Cathedral, 1891: Josiah Conder drew it from a Russian design. Its dome fell in the 1923 earthquake and was rebuilt smaller in 1929.
From the hill it looked over the whole of Tokyo once. Now look how the towers have grown round it.
Is the junk-parts shop still down that lane?
